extracted.name: Egg chops
extracted.description: As the sun sets and the call to Maghrib prayers fills the air, the heart longs for something warm, comforting, and deeply satisfying. During Ramadan, food is more than just nourishment—it’s a moment of gratitude, togetherness, and revival after a long day of fasting. Among the many snacks that grace the iftar table, egg chops hold a special place, just like pakoras. Egg chops are simple yet soulful. Boiled eggs are gently enclosed in a flavourful mashed potatoes mixture, coated in flour, egg and breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried until golden and crisp on the outside, while remaining soft and flavourful inside. Each bite is a perfect balance of crunch and comfort. Served hot with green chutney or a squeeze of lemon, egg chops instantly awaken the senses. Paired with a cup of chai, alongside dates and fruit chaat, they complete the iftar spread beautifully. In Ramadan, even the simplest dishes feel special when made with love. Egg chops may be humble, but on the iftar table, they become a reminder that comfort often lies in the simplest flavours.
instruction_lines: Heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat in a pan and sauté the onion till translucent.
Add the garlic and fry till raw smell is eliminated.
Add chilli flakes, salt, turmeric and lemon zest, Mix well, remove and allow to cool.
To the mashed potatoes add the cooled onion mixture; season with pepper powder and cilantro. Gently mash the mixture to combine the masala.
Beat the eggs with salt, season flour with salt and season the bread crumbs.
Take a mixture of the mashed potatoes and flatten it on the palm.
Place a sliced egg, yolk side down, enclose the egg, ensuring there are no crack.
Coat the eggs with flour, dip in egg and coat with bread crumbs. Reshape and place on a tray.
Heat oil over medium heat. Dip a skewer in oil and once bubbles rise, deep fry the eggs till golden. Remove to a wire rack.
